sources.quote: Statistics Canada put sales at food services and drinking places at $101.4 billion in 2025, up about 5.6 percent from 2024
sources.title: The Daily — Food services and drinking places, December 2025
sources.evidence: Annual sales of food services and drinking places totalled $101.4 billion in 2025, up 5.6% from 2024.

sources.quote: British Columbia's Food Delivery Service Fee Act, in force since January 2023, is the first permanent cap in Canada
sources.title: First permanent delivery-fee cap in Canada will help B.C. ring in new year
sources.evidence: Canada's first permanent cap on fees charged to restaurants by food-delivery companies went into effect in British Columbia on January 1, 2023. B.C. became the first province in Canada, and one of a handful of jurisdictions in North America, to implement a permanent cap on fees charged by food-delivery companies.

sources.quote: In Ontario, qualifying prepared food and beverages sold for $4.00 or less before tax have the 8 percent provincial portion of HST rebated at the till
sources.title: Harmonized Sales Tax for Ontario - Point-of-Sale Rebate on Prepared Food and Beverages - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: When qualifying prepared food sold for $4.00 or less is purchased, the vendor collects only the 5% federal part of the HST and pays or credits the rebate of the 8% provincial part of the HST to the consumer at the point of sale.

sources.quote: Ontario's Healthy Menu Choices Act, 2015 requires chains with 20 or more Ontario locations to post calories for every standard item
sources.title: Calories on menus: information for businesses | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: Beginning January 1st, 2017, the Healthy Menu Choices Act, 2015 and regulation (O. Reg. 50/16) require food service premises with 20 or more locations in Ontario to display calories on menus for standard food items.

sources.quote: The Competition Tribunal ordered Cineplex to pay $38.9 million in 2024 over an online booking fee, upheld on appeal in January 2026
sources.title: Statement from the Acting Commissioner of Competition on appeal court's ruling in Cineplex deceptive marketing case - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: On January 21, 2026, the Federal Court of Appeal dismissed Cineplex's appeal, with costs. The Competition Tribunal found that Cineplex engaged in drip pricing by adding a mandatory $1.50 online booking fee and ordered Cineplex to pay a financial penalty of over $38.9 million dollars and legal costs.

sources.quote: The Competition Act has expressly prohibited drip pricing since June 2022
sources.title: Competition Bureau wins deceptive marketing case against Cineplex - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Amendments to the Competition Act came into force on June 24, 2022, which explicitly recognize drip pricing as a harmful business practice. Drip pricing involves offering low prices to attract consumers but then adding mandatory fees so that the prices are unattainable.

sources.quote: Ontario's AGCO allows happy hour and price advertising but sets minimum prices, about $2.00 per standard drink
sources.publisher: Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.title: Pricing and Promotion of Liquor | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario
sources.evidence: A 12 oz beer or a 5 oz glass of wine may not be sold for less than $2, including taxes. A 1 oz drink containing spirits may not be sold for less than $1.34, including taxes. A licensee may vary the purchase price of liquor as long as it remains above the minimum price, whether offered in combination with food or other goods or services, or for a specified time.

sources.quote: Under the CRA's digital economy rules in force since July 1, 2021, platform operators are generally expected to register for GST/HST
sources.title: GST/HST for digital-economy businesses: Overview - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: The ETA has been amended, effective July 1, 2021, to include GST/HST provisions that generally apply to non-resident suppliers, distribution platform operators and accommodation platform operators participating in the digital economy. Measures for digital-economy businesses are in effect as of July 1, 2021.

flags.quote: 15 percent for core delivery service plus a maximum of 5 percent in other fees
flags.issue: The permanent BC cap under the Food Delivery Service Fee Regulation (B.C. Reg. 249/2022) is 20 percent of the order value for core delivery services, with an additional 5 percent cap on other related fees. The 15 percent figure was the temporary pandemic-era cap, not the permanent one in force since January 1, 2023.

flags.quote: about $2.00 per standard drink before HST, and bans all-you-can-drink offers
flags.issue: AGCO's Registrar's guidelines state the $2.00 minimum for a 12 oz beer or 5 oz glass of wine (and $1.34 for a 1 oz spirit serving) is a price including all applicable taxes, not a before-HST price.
